CARD_REWARD.when: The deck already has several strong attacks or adequate damage and scaling, but still relies mainly on starter Defends or lacks meaningful mitigation; HP is declining or defense is needed for upcoming fights.
CARD_REWARD.guidance: Favor meaningful Block, mitigation, draw, survival, or hybrid rewards, or skip, rather than adding another ordinary attack. Reassess attack-over-defense choices such as Carnage over Ghostly Armor or Whirlwind over Iron Wave. Stop reinforcing attack density unless a new attack fills a specific scaling plan or solves an imminent threat.
CARD_REWARD.rationale: Cleave and Twin Strike increased attack density while HP fell from 85/85 to 35/85, and the final deck had 15 attacks but only 8 clear defensive or mitigation cards. At 32/80 HP, Second Wind deserved stronger consideration than Rampage, and continued attack-heavy drafting left HP at 11/80. In another run, Carnage and Whirlwind were chosen despite substantial existing damage, leaving a 19-card deck with four Defends and no added Block card.

CARD_REWARD.when: The deck already contains several mediocre or redundant defensive cards and a reward offers another such card alongside a high-impact attack or skip.
CARD_REWARD.guidance: Do not keep taking True Grit, Iron Wave, or similar low-impact defense merely because it provides some Block. Favor a meaningful damage option such as Carnage when legal, or skip if none of the choices materially improve the deck.
CARD_REWARD.rationale: Repeatedly choosing True Grit and Iron Wave increased deck size and defensive repetition without solving the damage problem; the final deck contained three True Grits and two Iron Waves alongside other defensive cards.

CARD_REWARD.when: The deck already has a functional package of exhaust, Block, draw, area damage, or other core engine pieces, particularly when Snecko Eye makes costs variable and additional cards are merely overlapping roles.
CARD_REWARD.guidance: Make skipping the default for marginal rewards. Avoid repeatedly adding the same role unless the card materially improves the engine, fills a clearly missing function, or solves an imminent threat; preserve draw quality and concentration on the strongest cards.
CARD_REWARD.rationale: The final 28-card deck contained three Shrug It Offs, three Pommel Strikes, two Disarms, and two True Grits despite already having Feel No Pain, Dark Embrace+, Burning Pact+, True Grit, Immolate+, Shockwave+, and multiple Shrug It Offs. Repeated overlapping rewards diluted access to the existing engine.

CARD_REWARD.guidance:
Your deck-building decisions are too focused on whether each individual card is locally useful. Build toward a coherent long-term deck plan instead. Before adding a card, identify what the current deck's damage plan, defense plan, scaling, draw/energy needs, and major weaknesses are. Add a card only when it meaningfully fills one of those needs, strengthens an existing synergy, or enables a clear new strategy; otherwise skip it. Do not keep adding generically good cards simply because each one can be justified individually.

In combat, preserve the full-turn sequence you planned. If you plan to use setup followed by defense, do not abandon the defensive part on the next decision unless the game state materially changes. When lethal is not available and an enemy is attacking, avoid preventable HP loss when available block can substantially reduce or fully mitigate that damage and extra damage does not meaningfully change the fight. In particular, do not spend the remaining energy on marginal attacks after already planning to block.

CARD_REWARD.guidance:
Your deck planning improved this run, but you are still not treating the weaknesses identified in your own deck plan as real priorities. When the deck plan identifies a critical missing role, especially long-term damage scaling, prioritize cards that directly solve that weakness over cards that are merely efficient incremental upgrades. For example, in Act 2 you explicitly identified Strength/scaling as the deck's main missing component, but still chose Sword Boomerang over Spot Weakness. Sword Boomerang only gives more immediate attack damage, while Spot Weakness directly addresses the scaling problem you had already identified. Do not let short-term card quality override the long-term need stated in your own plan.

As the deck becomes more complete, raise the threshold for adding another card. Once damage, defense, draw and AoE are already adequately covered, a card should only beat Skip if it materially solves a named weakness, significantly strengthens an existing synergy, or enables a clear new strategy. A card being somewhat useful is not enough. If the deck plan says the deck is already large or compact and the main weakness is scaling, additions such as Armaments that do not solve that weakness should usually lose to Skip.

Combat sequencing was much better this run. Continue committing to the full-turn sequence and use the cheapest sufficient defensive option. Before spending Apparition, Impervious or other limited defensive resources, calculate the actual incoming damage and the block that the planned sequence will generate. If ordinary block fully mitigates the attack, preserve the stronger limited resource; if ordinary block is insufficient, use the stronger defense rather than taking preventable damage. Base this on the actual mitigation calculation, not simply on whether multiple enemies are attacking.

COMBAT.when: At low or rapidly declining HP against one or more attacking enemies, especially with little or no Block, when HP is in single digits or the fight is a boss.
COMBAT.guidance: First check whether lethal damage can end the fight before the enemy attacks. If not, play enough immediate Block or other protection to survive before attacks, exhaust setup, debuffs, draw, or incremental setup. Do not spend energy on actions that displace a legal Defend+, True Grit, Shrug It Off, or comparable defense. Use small Block only when it meaningfully prevents damage, and use potions or amplification after immediate survival is addressed.
COMBAT.rationale: At 5 HP, repeated Defends and a late Ancient Potion left enemies alive, while against Book of Stabbing small Defends failed to solve the damage race. Against Hexaghost, Strike and Bash+ were chosen before available True Grit and Defend at 10/87 and 7/87 HP. In the final fight, Disarm+, Pommel Strike, and exhaust setup were prioritized while both Torch Heads attacked at 26/85 HP and 0 Block, leaving the player exposed despite legal Defend+ and other defensive cards.

COMBAT.when: Entrench is in hand while current Block is zero, especially at low HP against an attacking enemy.
COMBAT.guidance: Do not spend Entrench for zero value. First create Block, or choose another legal defensive, draw, or lethal-damage option; preserve energy for immediate protection or killing the threat.
COMBAT.rationale: Entrench multiplies existing Block and provides no immediate protection at zero Block. Spending two energy on it at 13 HP left only one energy and no Block, followed by a turn that reduced HP to 3.

EVENT.when: An event offers a permanent curse or other deck pollution for gold or a modest benefit, especially when there is no confirmed near-term removal plan, the deck already has curse/status burden, or the payoff has no concrete immediate use.
EVENT.guidance: Favor the non-curse or safer option unless the gold is urgently needed and curse removal is realistically available soon, or the alternative HP cost is genuinely unsafe. Avoid unnecessary dead draws and permanent deck dilution, particularly before a boss; if taking the curse, establish a concrete removal plan.
EVENT.rationale: Decay remained after Desecrate even though 78/80 HP could have survived the alternative 20 HP loss for 5 Max HP. Another curse was accepted for gold that was not later converted into demonstrated value, and Doubt remained in the final deck because an available shop removal was not purchased.

EVENT.when: An event offers gold in exchange for direct HP loss and the run already has substantial gold or faces several difficult combats before the boss.
EVENT.guidance: Prefer Leave unless the gold is urgently needed for a specific high-impact purchase. Treat optional HP-for-gold trades as poor risks when survivability is the limiting resource.
EVENT.rationale: Touch cost 8 HP for 75 gold when the run already had 164 gold, reducing the buffer for remaining Act 1 fights; the run later entered the boss at 48 HP and finished at 1 HP.

Preserve enough energy for the strongest available attack or defensive line, especially when the enemy's block is already low or an orb can be finished.
37/48 hp should be sufficient to survive combat, do not need to rest if hp % is high.
taking random rare card is better than 100 gold for neow's blessing

REST.when: At a campfire or recovery event with substantially reduced or not comfortably high HP, especially at a later or final campfire before an elite or boss, when the deck already has a functional upgraded or offense-heavy core and lacks reliable potion support.
REST.guidance: Treat healing as the default emergency recovery. Prefer resting, sleeping, or equivalent recovery over a marginal upgrade or optional reward unless a clearly necessary upgrade is required to survive the imminent fight; preserve enough HP buffer for the remaining path and boss.
REST.rationale: Smithing at 57/80 and 62/85 HP was followed by major HP losses to Gremlin Nob, while resting at 35/85 and 11/80 provided substantially safer combat buffers. Entering Hexaghost at 64/87 after upgrading Shockwave led to death; the deck had enough damage to reduce the boss to 58 HP, suggesting additional entry HP was more valuable than the marginal upgrade. At 55/80 HP, smithing Carnage instead of resting left only 39/80 HP for the final Sentry combat in a run with no potions.
